about: Confusion pairs (W17). kind: sense (two senses of one headword; a plain headword such as "temper" names its everyday sense, given in the entry's everyday field), lookalike (alike in form or sound, unlike in meaning) or nearmiss (close in meaning, and the SAT sets one against the other). words are library slugs, or plain words that are not library entries. tell is the one line that separates them. Entries' own lookalikes are derived by the build and are not repeated here.

entries.tell: As an adjective, abstract means existing only as an idea; as a noun, an abstract is the short summary printed before a research article.
An apparent flaw may be plain to see or may only seem real; if the passage hints the look misleads (her apparent calm hid panic), it is the seeming sense.
Land or stock that appreciates rises in value, with no object; to appreciate a problem is to grasp how serious it is.
Assets appreciate by rising in price; people appreciate a favor by being grateful for it.
To appreciate the difficulty of a task is to understand it fully, not to be thankful for it.
Assume that something is true and you suppose it without proof; assume a role, a duty or a name and you take it on.
To compromise safety, health or one's principles is to weaken or endanger them; to compromise with a rival is to settle by each side giving ground.
Muscles, metals and economies contract by shrinking; people contract an illness by catching it.
A contract is a signed agreement, but a market or a metal that contracts simply becomes smaller.
To contract measles is to catch it; nothing is signed or agreed.
A curious person is eager to learn; a curious detail or habit is strange. Ask whether the word describes someone's interest or something's oddness.
Defer a decision and you put it off; defer to an expert and you give way to her judgment. The word to marks the yielding sense.
To elaborate on a point (verb) is to add detail; an elaborate plan (adjective) is intricate, with many parts.
People endure hardship by putting up with it; a tradition that endures simply lasts. With an object it is withstand; without one, last.
To grant a request or a license is to give it formally; to grant that a point is true is to admit it before arguing further.
Keen on or keen to means eager; a keen eye, ear or mind is sharp and quick to notice.
Maintain a road or a machine and you keep it in working order; maintain that a claim is true and you insist on it.
A modest person does not boast; a modest gain, budget or house is merely small.
The adjective objective means unbiased and based on facts; the noun an objective is a goal to reach.
The verb obscure means hide or cloud (fog obscured the peak); an obscure poet is little known.
A partial list is incomplete; a partial referee favors one side. Partial to someone also means fond of them.
Peculiar on its own usually means odd; peculiar to means belonging only to, as a plant peculiar to one island.
A prompt reply comes without delay (adjective); to prompt a reply is to cause it (verb).
To qualify a claim is to narrow it with a condition or exception; to qualify for a prize is to meet its requirements.
To render something useless is to make it so; to render a scene, a song or a role is to portray or perform it.
To resolve a dispute (verb) is to settle it; a person's resolve (noun) is firm determination.
To sanction a plan is to approve it officially; sanctions imposed on a country are penalties. The verb usually approves; the plural noun punishes.
To stem a flow is to stop it; to stem from a cause is to arise from it. The word from is the tell.
A field, an experiment or a search yields something by producing it; a person yields to pressure by giving way.
To temper criticism with praise is to soften it; a temper is a tendency to get angry.
To champion a cause is to fight for it; a champion is the winner of a contest.
To arrest a decline or a disease is to halt it; police arrest a suspect by taking him into custody.
A command of a language or a subject is mastery of it; a command is an order to be obeyed.
To check inflation or an advance is to hold it back; to check an answer is to make sure it is right.
A voice that betrays nervousness reveals it without meaning to; betraying a friend is being disloyal.
To entertain an idea or a doubt is to consider it; to entertain guests is to amuse them.
A grave error or threat is very serious; a grave is a burial place.
The verb intimate (IN-tuh-mate) means hint at; the adjective intimate (IN-tuh-mit) means close and personal.
As a verb, to occasion a change is to bring it about; as a noun, an occasion is an event or a time.
Pedestrian prose or ideas are dull and ordinary; a pedestrian is a person traveling on foot.
To reflect on a choice is to think carefully about it; a mirror reflects light.
Reservations about a plan are doubts; a reservation at a hotel is a booking.
A sound argument or method is well reasoned and reliable; a sound is a noise.
Spare prose or decor is plain and lean; a spare key or tire is extra.
To subject samples to heat is to make them undergo it; a subject is a topic or a person under study.
A plan found wanting is lacking or not good enough; wanting a thing is desiring it.
In the wake of an event means in its aftermath; to wake is to stop sleeping.
To advance a theory or an argument is to put it forward; troops advance by moving forward.
To air a grievance or a view is to express it publicly; to air a room is to let fresh air in.
To coin a word or phrase is to invent it; a coin is a piece of metal money.
A request couched in polite terms is phrased that way; a couch is a sofa.
To credit a discovery to someone is to attribute it to that person; to credit an account is to add money to it.
To execute a plan or a design is to carry it out; to execute a prisoner is to put him to death.
To exercise caution, power or a right is to use it; to exercise is to work out.
To fashion a tool out of bone is to shape or make it; fashion is the current style in clothing.
To field questions or complaints is to deal with them as they come; a field is open land.
Interest or energy that flags is weakening; to flag an error is to mark it for attention.
A plan or a ship that founders fails or sinks; a founder is a person who starts an organization.
The gravity of a situation is its seriousness; gravity is also the force that pulls objects toward the ground.
To harbor doubts or a grudge is to hold it privately in mind; a harbor is a port for ships.
To hold that a claim is true is to maintain it; to hold a cup is to grasp it.
Experience that informs an artist's work shapes it; to inform someone is to tell them facts.
A marked change or difference is clearly noticeable; a marked box has a mark written on it.
Minute (my-NOOT) means extremely small; a minute (MIN-it) is sixty seconds.
A moving speech stirs the emotions; a moving train is in motion.
To negotiate a steep trail or an obstacle is to get through it; to negotiate a deal is to bargain.
Critics who pan a film criticize it harshly; a camera that pans sweeps across a scene.
A pressing need or question is urgent; pressing a button is pushing down on it.
To realize a goal or an ambition is to achieve it; to realize a fact is to become aware of it.
To rehearse old arguments or grievances is to repeat or recount them; actors rehearse to practice.
To shoulder a cost or a duty is to take on the burden; to shoulder past someone is to push aside with the body.
In American usage, to table a proposal is to set it aside for later; a table is a piece of furniture.
To tender a resignation or a bid is to offer it formally; tender care is gentle.
To venture a guess or an opinion is to offer it cautiously; a venture is a risky undertaking.
To weather a storm or a crisis is to come through it; rock that has weathered has been worn away by exposure.
A scientific bent is a natural inclination toward science; a bent nail is curved.
A conviction is a firm belief; in court, a conviction is a verdict of guilty.
To discount a rumor or a warning is to treat it as unimportant; to discount a price is to lower it.
A fine distinction is subtle or precise; feeling fine means feeling okay.
A fluid situation is likely to change; a fluid is a liquid or a gas.
To husband resources is to use them sparingly; a husband is a married man.
To mount a campaign or an exhibit is to organize and begin it; to mount a horse is to climb onto it.
A stock phrase or character is standard and predictable; stock is shares in a company or goods kept on hand.
A task that taxes one's patience strains it; a tax is money owed to a government.
A novel's treatment of a theme is the way it handles that theme; medical treatment is care for an illness.
An account of an event is an explanation or a report of it; a bank account is a record of money held.
To conduct a study or a survey is to carry it out; to conduct an orchestra is to lead it.
A cool reception is unfriendly or unenthusiastic; in casual speech, cool means impressive.
A critical step or moment is crucial; a critical review finds fault.
A retiring person is shy and avoids attention; a retiring worker is ending a career.
A scientist's standing is her status or reputation; standing is also being on one's feet.
The verb appropriate (-ate) means take for one's own use, often without permission; the adjective appropriate (-it) means suitable.
An express promise or purpose is clearly stated; an express train makes few stops.
A patent falsehood is obvious; a patent is a legal right to an invention.
The moon waxes as it grows; to wax a floor is to polish it. Wax is the opposite of wane.
Critics who hail a book praise it publicly; to hail a taxi is to call out to it.
Lean years or harvests are meager; to lean on a wall is to rest against it.
Grounds for a complaint are the reasons for it; the ground is the surface of the earth.
In the SAT sense, plastic means easily shaped, as a young brain is plastic; everyday plastic is a synthetic material.
To dwell on a mistake is to keep thinking or talking about it; to dwell in a place is to live there.
A discriminating reader judges quality well; discriminating against people is treating them unfairly.
An arresting image is striking and holds attention; arresting a suspect is taking him into custody.
To act with dispatch is to act with speed and efficiency; to dispatch a messenger is to send him off.
